text:
marta: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector change that landed yesterday we see a weird p99 regression on Llama-2-13B for mid-sized batches (batch 4-8) at context ~3k. Not a steady slope — spikes every ~200 requests.

ian: Repro steps?

marta: Ran the nightly perf sweep: `./scripts/run_sweep.py --model llama-2-13b --contexts 512,1024,2048,3072 --batches 1,2,4,8 --kernel auto`

marta: Attach snippet from the flame graph sampler (shortened):
```
time  kernel   cpu%
0.00  attn_opt  12.1
0.01  matmul_gem 38.5
0.02  kv_store   21.4
0.03  attn_fallback 23.0  <-- correlated with spikes
```

dani: That attn_fallback line looks like the selector is flipping to a slower attention kernel intermittently. Any pattern in sequence length or head dim?

marta: Good call — it's correlated with requests where effective seq_len (prompt + gen) crosses ~2048 boundary and when head_dim % 64 != 0 (we saw most on some fine-tuned variants with head_dim 48/56).

ben: Interesting. Could be an alignment/tiling mismatch in the optimized kernel that triggers a fallback. Did you capture the kernel selector logs? `KERNEL_TRACE=1` should show selection decisions.

marta: Pasted an anonymized excerpt: 
```
[12:34:01] selector: model=llama-2-13b seq=1980 head_dim=48 hw=A100 kernel=attn_opt
[12:34:01] selector: model=llama-2-13b seq=2060 head_dim=48 hw=A100 kernel=attn_fallback
[12:34:02] selector: model=llama-2-13b seq=1998 head_dim=64 hw=V100 kernel=attn_opt
[12:34:03] selector: model=llama-2-13b seq=3072 head_dim=48 hw=32-core kernel=attn_fallback
```

ian: So both seq and head_dim factor. We changed the kernel threshold logic to prefer opt when predicted runtime < fallback+10% based on microbench; maybe the estimator is off for non-64-aligned head dims.

dani: Also saw some KV cache churn in the same window? ops-bot shows a small eviction log: `KV_EVICT: client=redwood-qa reason=batch_boundary` repeated. That could interact with selector due to extra memcpy and push kernel over threshold.

ops-bot: KV_EVICT events (count=12) in last 15m. Top cause: batch-boundary + prefix-sharing disabled.

ben: Action items I recommend: 1) add a quick guard to prefer fallback only when fallback advantage > 20% to reduce flip-flopping; 2) add head_dim alignment penalty to estimator; 3) run microbench for head_dim in {32,48,56,64} across seq lengths around boundary (1800-2200).

marta: I ran microbench (attached numbers):
```
head_dim=48 seq=1980 -> attn_opt 6.9ms, fallback 9.1ms
head_dim=48 seq=2060 -> attn_opt 10.5ms, fallback 8.7ms  <-- selector currently picks opt -> bad
head_dim=64 seq=2060 -> attn_opt 7.2ms, fallback 8.1ms
```

marta: Looks like estimator inversion at 2060 for head_dim=48 (opt slower due to tiling remainder). That explains spike pattern.

ian: Can we patch estimator weights quickly? If we add a head_dim % 64 penalty and a hysteresis (avoid switching for N requests), should stop the oscillation. Dani, any objections?

dani: sounds good. Also toggle `prefix_sharing=true` in the sweep to reduce KV_EVICT churn during tests — that'll decouple eviction noise.

ben: I'll draft a tiny selector hotfix: add 1.15x multiplier when head_dim % 64 != 0 and require 20% predicted improvement to switch. Quick rollback path too.

marta: After applying a local patch with 1.15x penalty + 20% threshold, my p99 dropped back to baseline in the same sweep. Will run a full-nightly.

ian: Great. Follow-up: add a long-term task to expand microbench matrix (head_dim 32-128 step 8, seq 256-8192 step 256) and persist results to the kernel profile DB so selector uses empirical table instead of heuristic.

dani: Filing a ticket for the matrix + KV policy coordination. Tagging infra for collector retention increase. :thumbsup:

marta: TL;DR — regression caused by selector flip for non-64-aligned head dims near 2k seq boundary + KV eviction noise. Hotfix applied (penalty+hysteresis) — nightly tests in progress.

ben: Nice triage. If nightly is green, roll the hotfix to staging and enable canary at 5% for Dedicated clusters.

ops-bot: Deploy job queued: rollout/hotfix-selector -> staging (canary 5%).

marta: Thanks all — will update with final sweep numbers tomorrow.
